questions.question: Use the particle model to explain what happens when ice melts, why energy is absorbed, and why the temperature stays at 0 °C while it melts.
questions.expected_answer: In ice the water particles vibrate about fixed positions in a regular arrangement, held by strong forces. Heating gives them more energy, so they vibrate more strongly. At the melting point (0 °C) they have enough energy to break free of their fixed positions and slide past one another while staying close together, so the solid becomes a liquid. Energy must be absorbed to overcome the forces holding the particles in place. While melting is happening, all the energy supplied goes into freeing particles from their fixed positions rather than making them move faster, so the temperature stays at 0 °C until all the ice has melted.

questions.question: Give three differences between evaporation and boiling, explain why evaporation cools a liquid, and explain why water boils at about 94 °C in Johannesburg.
questions.expected_answer: Evaporation happens only at the surface, boiling happens throughout the liquid with bubbles of vapour; evaporation happens at any temperature, boiling only at the boiling point; evaporation is slow and quiet, boiling is rapid. Evaporation cools because the fastest particles escape, so the average energy of the particles left behind falls. Johannesburg is about 1 750 m above sea level, where air pressure is lower, so water boils at a lower temperature, about 94 °C, instead of 100 °C at sea level.

questions.question: Sketch and describe the heating curve of water from -20 °C ice to steam above 100 °C. Explain the flat sections and why a change of state is a physical change.
questions.expected_answer: Five parts: temperature rises from -20 °C to 0 °C (ice warming); flat at 0 °C while ice melts (solid and liquid present); rises from 0 °C to 100 °C (water warming); a longer flat section at 100 °C while water boils (liquid and gas present); rises above 100 °C (steam heating). On the flat sections the energy supplied overcomes the forces between particles instead of increasing their speed, so temperature is constant; the boiling plateau is longer because separating particles into a gas needs about seven times as much energy. A change of state is physical because no new substance forms: ice, water and steam are all water molecules, only their arrangement, movement and spacing change, the change is reversible, and mass is conserved.
